criteria.copy_identity_overlay: Author a browser-only copy of the whole assertion identity module with portable logic and stubbed hashing, leaving every canonical file untouched; the browser links the copy while the server keeps the original.
criteria.split_hashing_out: Move the two node:crypto hashing functions into their own server-only module, keeping all portable lineage functions shared; the four existing importers swap to the module they actually need and no behavior changes.

assert_chain.instructions: How should the node:crypto edge inside the shared assertion identity chain be repaired so browser builds stop reaching it?

criteria.gate_cookies: Reject all five cookie operations at check time for the browser profile and ship a stub alternate that only satisfies linking, because browser code has no catalogue source for cookie strings and cannot observe HttpOnly state.
criteria.portable_cookies: Reimplement cookie parsing, validation and serialization portably for the browser profile and keep all cookie operations available in both profiles.

cookie_scope.instructions: Should cookie operations stay available in the browser profile or be declared server-only?

criteria.canonical_timer_sink: Edit the shared clock and log modules to use setTimeout and console directly so both profiles run identical bytes.
criteria.overlay_timer_sink: Ship browser alternates for clock sleep via setTimeout and log writing via console, leaving the server modules byte-identical.

divergent_platforms.instructions: How should the natively implementable clock sleep and log sink divergences be resolved?

criteria.bundler_plugin: Give Bun.build a resolve plugin that redirects canonical runtime paths to their browser alternates during bundling, keeping the staged tree identical to the audited generation.
criteria.rewrite_staged_edges: Rewrite edges that resolve to overlaid canonical modules into alternate edges inside the staged bundler tree, so the bytes on disk are exactly what ships with no bundler plugins.

overlay_application.instructions: At bundle time, how should canonical runtime imports be redirected to their sealed browser alternates?

criteria.canonical_escape: Replace the native HTML escape calls in the shared module with a portable five-character escaper proven identical to the native one by exhaustive differential tests.
criteria.overlay_escape: Ship a browser alternate duplicating the HTML module with a portable escaper while the server keeps the native calls.

pure_escape.instructions: How should the pure HTML escaping helper used by browser-reachable code be made shippable?

criteria.admit_unused_host_ops: Leave the host operations in the reachable graph and rely on the bundler removing uncalled code and on production never invoking those paths.
criteria.portable_everything: Write portable browser implementations for TOML, YAML, JSON5, CSRF, Markdown and asset serving so every operation stays available in both profiles.
criteria.stub_and_gate: Ship minimal stub alternates through the sealed overlay for TOML, YAML, JSON5, CSRF, Markdown and asset serving, and reject those operations at check time with span evidence.

server_only_set.instructions: How should browser-reachable operations with no browser-native implementation be handled?

state.audit_contract: The structural browser audit scans every module reachable from the browser root through value edges. Quoted host names pass, but any executed Bun, process, require, eval, Function, dynamic import, or node and bun edge fails the build, and the auditor must never trust the bundler to drop uncalled code. Sealed profile alternates substitute for canonical modules during traversal.
state.blockers: A verified reachability closure over the module inventory finds 59 runtime modules reachable from the browser root. Host operations remain in codec formats (Bun TOML, YAML, JSON5), cookies (Bun Cookie), CSRF (Bun CSRF), clock (Bun sleep), log (Bun stderr write), HTML (Bun escapeHTML at six sites), Markdown (Bun markdown engine), assets (Bun file disk read), and assertion identity (node:crypto through context, barrier and queue chains). The audit task recorded this as residual risk for later repair.
state.browser_needs: Browser programs use clock, log and HTML rendering. They have no catalogue operation producing cookie header strings, no CSRF secret, no Markdown or TOML consumers, and the browser serves no asset routes; the server reads the HttpOnly session cookie instead.
state.limits: The check and emit packages are frozen under a concurrent owner, so state factory imports cannot be pruned there. There are zero external users and no compatibility obligation. The sealed overlay table and the check-time capability gate accept additions. Server behavior must keep passing its tests, and one lane concurrently owns the canonical asset and server modules.
